deadline.value: Applications are accepted all year, and should normally arrive by the end of June for an October start, but funding deadlines come much earlier. The President's PhD Scholarship rounds (open to Indian applicants) close 2 Nov 2026, 11 Jan 2027 and 1 Mar 2027; EPSRC DTA applicants (UK/EU residents) should apply by 1 April.
deadline.quote: Applicants who apply by 23:59 (UK time) 2 November 2026 and are awarded a scholarship will be notified by 31 January 2027. | Applicants who apply by 23:59 (UK time) 11 January 2027 | Applicants who apply by 23:59 (UK time) 1 March 2027

also.quote: Normally, an application should be received at least by the end of June if it is to be processed in time for entry the following October. However, we do accept applications through the year.

supervisor.value: Before applying, you must contact academic staff to discuss the project, your eligibility and funding, and name the supervisor who supports you. Applications without a prospective supervisor's support cannot be processed.
supervisor.quote: It is essential that you contact the relevant member(s) of academic staff to discuss the project you are interested in, and to discuss eligibility and funding, before you submit your formal application to the College. Unfortunately, we are not able to process applications which do not have the support of a prospective supervisor, who should be clearly named in the application.

funding.value: The department's roughly 5 EPSRC DTA studentships a year are for UK/EU applicants who meet residency rules. Overseas applicants rely on project studentships from individual academics or on competitive college, external and international scholarships.
funding.quote: The Department usually has approximately 5 competitive Doctoral Training Award (DTA) full studentships from the EPSRC each year, for UK and EU applicants who meet the requirements. | Prospective students are also able to apply for various College, external and international scholarships.

entry_route.value: You usually need a 2:1 or first (or equivalent) bachelor's plus a master's in mechanical engineering, aeronautics, materials science, mathematics or another relevant science or engineering subject.
entry_route.quote: We usually require applicants to hold a 2:1 or 1st (or equivalent) at undergraduate level and a Master’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Aeronautics, Materials Science, Mathematics, or other relevant science/ engineering subjects.

toefl_min.value: Mechanical Engineering requires Imperial's Standard English level: TOEFL iBT 92 overall (min 20 in each section), or 4.5 on the new scale.
toefl_min.quote: Students are required to achieve the College’s Standard level of attainment in English language before registration.

ielts_min.value: Mechanical Engineering requires Imperial's Standard English level: IELTS Academic 6.5 overall (min 6.0 in each element).
ielts_min.quote: Students are required to achieve the College’s Standard level of attainment in English language before registration.

notes: The department recruits about 60 PhD students a year. Your research proposal should be agreed with your supervisor before you apply. Aeronautics is a separate Imperial department with its own PhD, not covered here.
